approach: Add a `bug-evidence` entry to defaults.toml. Add `ensure_bug_evidence(reading, request_text)` in reading.rs beside `ensure_changelog`, called from `build_reading` before `validate()`. For a `change` reading whose title, summary or request text names a bug, wrong output, regression or slowdown (whole-word match), it appends one content criterion demanding data-backed root-cause evidence and one `bug-evidence` defaults_applied entry. It is idempotent and adds nothing for other readings. To thread the request text, `build_reading` gains a `request_text: &str` argument, passed from its one production caller (`request.text`, reading.rs:642-651). Add tests in athena-core, athena-data and athena-context. The new reader line pushes the reader set (1997 of 2000 tokens) over its budget. That budget is a constant in `BudgetSet::budget` (crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:175) and is not in athena.toml, so the addition is paid for inside defaults.toml by moving the first sentence break in three existing defaults. The `budget reader` line in docs/system-facts.md is then updated to the measured value. CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/defaults-loop.md record the change and its cause.

decisions.choice: Add the criterion and defaults entry in `build_reading`, as a new step next to `ensure_changelog`, not as a refusal in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: The goal is that bug jobs carry a criterion the final verdict can judge. The root cause was that no criterion demanded data-backed root-cause evidence (the final verdict rejected claims with none). A step that adds the criterion guarantees it without a model round trip. It refuses nothing, so there is no refusal rate to replay and no new `step!` line or corpus case. It follows the `ensure_changelog` pattern: idempotent, and runs before `validate()`.

rejected.option: A `check_*` refusal in `refusing_check` that rejects a bug reading lacking the criterion
rejected.why: It adds a refusal rule (replay share, a corpus case that must refuse, `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`) and sends the reader round again for a fixed sentence Athena can write itself.

rejected.option: Rely on the reader prompt and the new default alone
rejected.why: Prose-only. The `mechanism` default asks for enforcement by mechanism, and the reader already skipped such criteria.

decisions.choice: Detect bug-type work from the reading's title and summary plus the request text, with whole-word matching (reuse `has_phrase`, reading.rs:4058) on `bug`, `bugs`, `regression(s)`, `wrong output`, `wrong-output`, `slowdown(s)`. Apply only when `capability == Some("change")`, as `ensure_changelog` does.
decisions.reason: `class_of_work` is a closed list (athena.toml:129) with no bug class, so the class cannot tell. The reader may paraphrase ("Fix the crash"), so the request text is also read. `build_reading` has no request today, so one `&str` argument is added; it has one production caller (reading.rs:642) with `request.text` in scope, plus the test helper `build_sized` (reading.rs:5630). Study and decline readings start no producer, so they get nothing.

rejected.option: Match only the reading's title, summary and criteria, with no request argument
rejected.why: A terse request like "fix a bug in X" can be read into a summary with no keyword, so the step would miss it.

rejected.option: Add a `bug` class to `[classes]` in athena.toml
rejected.why: Adding a class is a job of its own (athena.toml:128), changes governance, and bug work is also code or tests.

decisions.choice: Idempotency by marker: add the defaults entry only if no entry has id `bug-evidence`, and add the criterion only if no criterion text starts with the constant's lead phrase.
decisions.reason: If the reader recorded the default but wrote no criterion, the criterion is still added. If the reader wrote its own wording, a second near-duplicate criterion is tolerated. The step runs twice safely.

rejected.option: Skip both when the defaults entry exists
rejected.why: A reader that lists the default but writes no criterion would escape the mechanism.

decisions.choice: The criterion is `kind: content`, with no file path, no `only ... may change` wording and no producer-report wording. Text: "Before any fix, the change states the root cause, shows it from data the job can read (records, a code path or a failing case) and shows why the wrong output or metric change follows from it; a guess labelled as an estimate does not meet this."
decisions.reason: A content criterion is judged from the diff the verifier sees. Checks that scan criteria (`producer_evidence_phrase`, `check_boundary_and_repo_files`, `limits_changed_files`) do not fire on it. `check_environment_reach` reads behavior criteria only (reading.rs:4777-4782). A newcomer can tell what evidence is required, which meets the outcome-check default.

rejected.option: A behavior criterion that names a command
rejected.why: No single command shows root-cause evidence in general, and a behavior criterion would trigger `check_code_survey` and `check_environment_reach`.

decisions.choice: Leave athena.toml unchanged. Pay for the new reader line by splitting the first sentence of the existing `buy-first`, `public` and `verified` defaults (change a `;`/`,` to `. `), in the order needed, and update the `budget reader` line in docs/system-facts.md. The `root-cause` default is not touched.
decisions.reason: The reading assumed the reader budget lives in athena.toml. It does not. It is `BudgetSet::Reader => 2_000` in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:175, and docs/system-facts.md says to update the line and never the budget. The reader set composes `defaults.render()` (reading.rs:216; budgets.rs:34-39), which shows only each first sentence (defaults.rs:55-69), so a shorter first sentence costs the reader fewer tokens. The full statement still reaches the producer and verifier through `get()` (briefs.rs:87-98, rendered at 284-296). Those sets compose only contract, frame and section, so they do not grow. No test pins these statements (searched). Tests do pin the `behavior-evidence`, `root-cause`, `outcome-check`, `no-empty-success` and `thrash-stop` lines, so those stay as they are.

rejected.why: The system-facts note and the `an_over_budget_role_set_fails` test say additions are paid for with removals. lib.rs is not a listed deliverable.
It is a pinned prompt frame (tests at lib.rs:440-449 and briefs.rs:4616-4630 match its wording) and not a listed deliverable.
No reader token budget is configured there; editing it would be a governance change with no effect.

decisions.reason: The `root-cause` and `behavior-evidence` entries were added at version 1. Only the proposals path raises the version (proposals.rs:88-96), and Athena never edits defaults.toml by itself (defaults-loop.md §9). Nothing reads the number to gate on it (searched).

rejected.why: It changes `Component::new("defaults", version, ..)` and recorded `defaults_version` for no behavioral need.

decisions.reason: Bug, wrong-output and regression are not classes in the closed list. `*` is also the shortest rendering (`[*]`), which saves reader tokens. The first sentence names the work it covers.

rejected.option: List classes such as code and tests
rejected.why: It costs about 10 more bytes in the reader line and wrongly implies the default is class-bound.

files.purpose: Add `[[default]] id = "bug-evidence"`, `applies_to = ["*"]`, a short first sentence and a statement that requires the root cause, its evidence from readable data and why the symptom follows, before any fix, and says an estimate-labelled guess does not meet it. Its `source` cites 20261104-054700-e6js, 20261105-051344-q9fv, 20261105-101121-qw9r and 20261105-205835-hk09 as jobs whose root-cause claims had no readable data and were rejected at the final verdict. Make the minimum number of first-sentence splits in `buy-first`, `public` and `verified` needed to keep the reader set at or under 2000 tokens. `root-cause` is not touched.

Add the `build_for_request` test helper and the `bug_evidence_*` tests.

risks.risk: The reader set is 3 tokens under its budget, so the new line fails `every_role_set_is_within_its_budget` until it is paid for. The exact savings are an estimate (about 55 to 70 bytes per split, from reading the current text) and were not measured.
risks.mitigation: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` after the defaults.toml edit. Split the `buy-first`, `public` and `verified` sentences in turn, stopping as soon as the reader is at or under 2000. Write the measured size into docs/system-facts.md. Do not raise the budget.

risks.risk: False positives: a request that adds a regression test, or a summary that merely mentions a bug, gets the root-cause criterion. A request that says "crash" or "incorrect" with no listed word is missed.
risks.mitigation: Keep the keyword list narrow (whole words only), gate on the `change` capability, and add a negative-case table. The extra criterion is harmless to a job that already states its root cause, and the limit is documented in the doc comment and defaults-loop.md.

risks.risk: The added criterion text could trip an existing reading check (for example `producer_evidence_phrase` on "shows"/"names" near "the producer", or `limits_changed_files`) and refuse the reading.
risks.mitigation: The criterion is content kind with no path, no `only ... may change` phrase and no producer-report wording; `bug_evidence_added_text_trips_no_refusal_check` runs `refusing_check` on the built reading and fails if any check refuses.

risks.risk: The reader may record the default itself and write its own criterion, leaving two similar criteria.
risks.mitigation: Idempotency is checked per field (id for the entry, lead phrase for the criterion), with a test for a reader-supplied entry.

risks.risk: The step only guarantees the criterion exists, not that the producer meets it; the final verdict is still the verifier's judgement.
risks.mitigation: The step is the only place the new default is enforced. The doc comment and defaults-loop.md section 3.9 mark the verifier's final-verdict logic as out of scope and unchanged. The default statement says the evidence must be readable data.

risks.risk: The brief lists athena.toml as a deliverable, but this plan does not change it, and docs/system-facts.md is changed but unlisted.
risks.mitigation: The producer lists the changed paths in its report; the reader's deliverables list already includes athena.toml with a low probability. The plan states why athena.toml is not edited.

open_questions: User: docs/system-facts.md is not in the deliverable list, but `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails unless its `budget reader` line changes. This plan edits only that line. Is that acceptable, or should the reader budget be raised in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs instead (against the file's own instruction not to raise a budget)?

User: To keep the reader set within 2000 tokens, the plan splits the first sentence of `buy-first`, `public` and `verified` in defaults.toml. The full statements the producer and verifier read stay the same in meaning, but the reader sees less of them. Is that acceptable, or should a different default shorten?

Host: reader_headroom and the budgets test count tokens as ceil(bytes/3). The exact bytes saved by each split can only be measured by running `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`, which the planner cannot run. The producer measures and splits only as many first sentences as it needs.
